sourcedFrom: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: This guide comes from Browning's own owner's manual for the BT-99 Plus. The Plus has its own book, separate from the base BT-99, because it is a different gun to care for. It has an adjustable rib, an adjustable cheek piece and a recoil reducer in the stock. It has a selective ejector, so a fired hull is thrown clear and a live shell is only lifted. It has no safety at all, so an open action is your safety. The field strip is two parts: the forearm comes off, then the barrel lifts off the hinge pin. The Plus book asks for a thin film of oil on the hand-fitted hinge surfaces, and it says to leave the recoil reducer alone and never oil it.

steps.title: Top lever right, action open
steps.action: Point the muzzle somewhere safe, down range if you are on the line, and keep your fingers off the trigger. Push the top lever to the right and pull the forearm down so the action breaks open. Browning built the Plus with no safety on purpose, for trap. That means a closed, loaded Plus is ready to fire, and opening the action is the only way to make it safe.
steps.quote: Open the action by pushing the top lever to the right, as explained previously.
steps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — General Operating Procedures > UNLOADING, step 1
steps.warn: THE BT-99 PLUS SHOTGUN HAS NO MANUAL SAFETY.

steps.title: The ejector throws a hull, but only lifts a live shell
steps.action: The Plus has a selective ejector. When the action opens, a fired hull is thrown clear of the gun, but an unfired shell is only raised a little out of the chamber. So a breech that looks empty at a glance can still hold a live shell standing proud of the chamber. Tip the breech a little to the right, or to the left if you shoot left-handed, so a thrown hull goes away from your face. Then lift out any raised shell with your fingers and put it away from where you will clean.
steps.quote: The BT-99 Plus has an automatic, selective ejector.
steps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — General Operating Procedures > UNLOADING, step 2

steps.title: Look into the chamber and through the barrel
steps.action: Now look. Check the chamber, then look through the barrel from the breech end to be sure there is no shell and nothing lodged in the bore. Browning wants this check every time the gun comes out of its case or off a rack, not only before cleaning. Keep all ammunition away from the bench before you go on.
steps.quote: When you retrieve your gun from its case or from a gun rack, always immediately open the action and check to assure that no shells are in the chambers.
steps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — No Manual Safety
steps.warn: BEFORE PERFORMING ANY CLEANING PROCEDURES, ALWAYS MAKE CERTAIN THERE ARE NO SHELLS IN THE CHAMBERS.

steps.title: Close it, brace the stock, pull the latch out
steps.action: With the gun empty, close the action. Rest the buttstock against your upper leg so the gun is held steady and pointed away. Pull the takedown lever latch on the underside of the forearm outward. The action must be closed for this. The forearm locks onto the barrel, and it has to come off before the barrel can.
steps.quote: With the action closed, anchor the gun's buttstock against your upper leg and pull the takedown lever latch outward.
steps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 1

steps.title: Pivot the forearm away and set it aside
steps.action: Keep the latch pulled out and hold the forearm with the rest of your left hand. With your right hand helping, swing the forearm away from the barrel until it comes free, then set it aside. It pivots off. It does not slide off. If it will not move, check that the latch is fully out instead of pulling harder.
steps.quote: With the help of your right hand, pivot the forearm away from the barrel (See Figure 9). Set the forearm aside.
steps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 2

steps.title: Open the action, lift the barrel off the hinge pin
steps.action: Break the action open the normal way with the top lever. The barrel is now held only by its lug sitting on the hinge pin. Unhook the lug from the pin gently and lift the barrel up and out of the action. The lug and the hinge pin are hand-fitted. Knocking them together is what marks them.
steps.quote: Carefully disengage the barrel lug from the hinge pin and lift the barrels upward out of the action.
steps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 4

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have the action with the buttstock, the barrel, and the forearm. Browning says a light cleaning can be done with the barrel on, but a full cleaning needs exactly this. From here the cleaning covers the bore and chamber, the choke tube, the ports if your barrel has them, the hinge pin, the barrel lug and the forearm bracket. It also covers the adjustable rib and the cheek piece hardware.
steps.quote: A full cleaning requires that you remove the barrels and forearm.
steps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning Suggestions
steps.warn: Remember the broad, polished, finely fitted surfaces of the receiver and forearm mechanisms (the barrel lugs, the hinge pin and forearm bracket) must always have a thin film of oil.

deepSteps.title: Choke tube out with the wrench
deepSteps.action: With the gun empty and the action open, fit the Invector Plus wrench that came with the gun. Turn the tube counterclockwise to break it loose. Then twist it out the rest of the way with your fingers. The Plus uses Invector Plus tubes for back-bored barrels. They are not interchangeable with standard Invector tubes, so keep them apart.
deepSteps.quote: to loosen the tube, turning it counterclockwise. Finger twist the tube the rest of the way out of the barrel.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Invector Plus Choke Tube System > TUBE REMOVAL, step 3

deepSteps.title: Clean and oil both sets of threads
deepSteps.action: Look at the threads inside the muzzle and on the tube. Both must be clean before the tube goes back. Clean them, then give them a light coat of oil. Grit or dry threads are how a tube gets stuck or marks the barrel threads.
deepSteps.quote: Lightly oil the threads with an oil like Browning Oil.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Invector Plus Choke Tube System > TUBE INSTALLATION, step 3

deepSteps.title: Tube back in: fingers first, then the wrench
deepSteps.action: Screw the tube into the muzzle by hand, tapered end first and notched end out, until it is finger-tight. Then use the wrench to seat it firmly. Starting by hand is how you avoid cross-threading it. Never fire the Plus without a choke tube fitted, because Browning warns the threads can be permanently damaged.
deepSteps.quote: When it becomes finger-tight, use the Invector choke tube wrench to firmly seat the tube.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Invector Plus Choke Tube System > TUBE INSTALLATION, step 4
deepSteps.warn: THE INVECTOR CHOKE TUBE SHOULD BE PERIODICALLY CHECKED TO ENSURE THAT IT IS TIGHT AND FIRMLY SEATED.

deepSteps.title: Ported barrels: the ports themselves
deepSteps.action: Some Plus barrels have ports drilled in the top near the muzzle. If yours does, clean them with a rag soaked in powder solvent. Stubborn residue can be scraped out with a pipe cleaner, a small brush or a small screwdriver. Go carefully so you do not mar the bluing outside or scratch the bore inside. If your barrel is not ported, skip this step.
deepSteps.quote: If your shotgun has barrel ports, carefully clean them with a rag soaked in powder solvents.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning Suggestions > CLEANING PROCEDURES, step 5

deepSteps.title: Rib off only if it needs it: raise the rear first
deepSteps.action: Browning says the rib rarely needs to come off, but it gives the steps for when it does need cleaning. First turn the rear elevation screw counterclockwise until the rear of the rib is as high as it will go. Do not force it. This screw is your point-of-impact setting, so you will have to set it again afterwards. Never try to lift the rib off at the front with the rear still down.
deepSteps.quote: Never attempt to remove the rib by lifting on the front of the rib without the rear rib adjustment fully raised.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Adjusting Point of Impact > REMOVING AND REINSTALLING THE RIB, steps 1 and 3

deepSteps.title: Tap out the front rib pin with the supplied punch
deepSteps.action: Hold the gun securely, in a padded vise if you have one, or on a surface that will not mar the finish. Use the rib punch that came with the Plus and a light hammer to tap out the roll pin at the front rib post. The punch is made for this, so it does not mark the rib. Note which of the rib's two holes the pin came out of. That hole is your muzzle-end setting.
deepSteps.quote: With the special BT-99 Plus rib punch (supplied) and a light hammer, tap out the pin holding the rib to the front rib post (See Figure 20).
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Adjusting Point of Impact > CHANGING THE POSITION OF THE RIB AT THE MUZZLE END, step 2

deepSteps.title: Lift the rib forward and out, keep the pivot
deepSteps.action: Lift the muzzle end of the rib up about 30 degrees, then lift the rib forward and out of the rear rib elevator housing. Watch the rib pivot. It is the small round part with a shoulder on each side, and it comes away easily. Leave the elevator detent spring in its groove. Browning says it does not need to come out. Clean the grit out of the rib parts and oil them lightly.
deepSteps.quote: With the rib removed be careful not to lose the rib pivot.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Adjusting Point of Impact > REMOVING AND REINSTALLING THE RIB, steps 3 to 5

deepSteps.title: Rib back on, pin back in, then reset the impact
deepSteps.action: Check the detent spring is in place and the elevation screw is fully counterclockwise. Put the rear of the rib into the elevator housing with the front raised about 30 degrees, pivot shoulders in the grooves. Lower the front onto the post and tap the roll pin back into the hole you noted, until no part of it sticks out on either side. Then turn the rear screw back to your point of impact. Each click is about half an inch at 40 yards.
deepSteps.quote: Make sure that the shoulders on the rib pivot are aligned with the grooves in the rear rib elevator housing.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Adjusting Point of Impact > REMOVING AND REINSTALLING THE RIB, step 6

deepSteps.title: Cheek piece off, adjustment parts wiped
deepSteps.action: Now and then, take the cheek piece off and wipe the parts under it. Loosen the two set screws on the right side of the cheek piece and lift it straight up off the studs. Wipe the studs and the hardware clean. Put it back on the studs and tighten the two set screws. Your drop at comb is held by the drop stop screw under the cheek piece, so leave that screw alone and the height comes back where it was.
deepSteps.quote: Occasionally remove the cheek piece and wipe the adjustment parts clean.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning Suggestions > OTHER CLEANING SUGGESTIONS

deepSteps.title: No further — Browning stops here
deepSteps.action: This is as far as Browning's book goes. It warns that the inner mechanism is finely fitted and can be permanently marred by taking it apart. The recoil reducer in the stock is sealed with grease from the factory. Do not oil it, because oil washes that grease away. For anything deeper, or any problem with the reducer, Browning sends you to a Browning Recommended Service Center, a competent gunsmith, or its service facility in Arnold, Missouri.
deepSteps.quote: NEVER ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR BT-99 PLUS APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS MANUAL.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Plus Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning Suggestions > OTHER CLEANING SUGGESTIONS
deepSteps.warn: In fact, attempting to oil it will wash away the lifetime lubrication already given it.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Barrel off the receiver, and the rod goes in from the breech end
A lightly oiled patch big enough to fit snugly, run back and forth several times
Look through the bore from both ends for lead and plastic streaks, usually near the muzzle and just ahead of the chamber
If the streaks are heavy, brass brush with powder solvent. Push the brush all the way through before you pull it back
Clean dry patch, then a final lightly oiled patch
Check that no patch is left in the barrel or chamber
Do not leave a fired hull in the chamber. Clean the chamber promptly after plastic shells

cleaning.name: HINGE & LOCKUP SURFACES
tasks: Wipe the receiver, forearm and barrel metal clean with a rag
One or two drops of oil on the forearm bracket
Oil on the barrel lug, hinge pin bearing surface, ejector slide and barrel flats
Oil on the hinge pin, cocking lever and locking bolt in the receiver
Keep a thin film of oil on the hinge pin, barrel lugs and forearm bracket. They are hand-fitted and should never run dry
Breech faces kept clean and lightly oiled. Grit here can stop the action from closing

cleaning.name: CHOKE & PORTS
tasks: Choke tube out, then the tube and the muzzle threads cleaned
Light oil on the tube and threads before it goes back in
Ported barrels: powder solvent on a rag through each port
Check now and then that the tube is still tight

cleaning.name: RIB & CHEEK PIECE
tasks: Clean grit from in and around the adjustable rib's front post and rear elevator. Aerosol oil helps
Only take the rib off if it needs it, and reset your point of impact afterwards
Now and then, lift off the cheek piece and wipe the studs and hardware clean

cleaning.name: STOCK & RECOIL REDUCER
tasks: Never oil the recoil reducer. Oil washes out its factory grease
Do not flood the action with oil. It runs back into the stock wood and loosens it
Wipe the wood with a light gun oil or a quality furniture polish, but not both

reassembly: Make sure the chamber is empty. Put one or two drops of oil on the forearm bracket, the barrel lug, hinge pin bearing surface, ejector slide and barrel flats, and the hinge pin, cocking lever and locking bolt.
Hold the pistol grip in your right hand with the buttstock anchored between your right forearm and your side. Push the top lever all the way right with your thumb.
With your left hand, set the barrel lug's round recess onto the action's hinge pin.
Keep pressure on the barrel so the pin stays in its recess, then swing the barrel up to close the action. Let go of the top lever and it should snap back.
Rest the butt on your upper leg. Set the back of the forearm against the front of the receiver.
Pivot the forearm up tight against the barrel until the takedown latch locks. The latch should sit flush with the wood under the forearm.
Never force the action closed. If something catches, start over and seat the barrel lug on the hinge pin again.
fncheck: First make sure the chamber is empty and point the muzzle somewhere safe. Open and close the action a few times. It should close without force, and you should let the top lever snap back on its own. Do not slow it with your thumb. It does not have to come back all the way to center. With the action closed, push the top lever lightly to the left to feel that the breech is fully shut. Try to wiggle the forearm. It should be tight on the barrel, with the latch flush. Check the choke tube is snug. If you took the rib off, check the front pin sits flush on both sides and the rib is back at your point of impact. Then leave the action open, the way Browning says a BT-99 Plus should sit when you are not on the line.
